newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Feb. 10.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Feb. 10.

text.p: All major Mexican ports were reported open Monday as the weather improved in the Gulf of Mexico, Communications and Transport Ministry said in its 1000 local/1600 GMT daily report.

Crude ports Dos Bocas and Pajaritos reopened to crude exports at 0645 local/1245 GMT and 0800 local/1400 GMT, repectively. The nation's largest crude port, Cayo Arcas, remained open amid the high wind velocities.
The ministry advised ships to exercise caution along the coasts of Tamaulipas, Veracruz and Tabasco states and in the Gulf of Tehuantepec because of strong winds and high waves.
Smaller ships, such as fishing and tourism boats, were restricted from sailing at Alvarado and Frontera ports, where winds blew at up to 30 km per hour.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.
Some clouds and winds about 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 17 miles per hour), except in the Gulf of Tehuantepec, where winds were reported at up to 38 km/22 miles per hour.
A cold front moving down coastline causing rains along coast of Sonora and lower temperatures.
-- Gulf of Mexico: Lower temperatures along northern

coast of Tamaulipas and light rains along Tamaulipas, Veracruz and Tabasco coasts. Winds from east and northeast of 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/17 to 22 miles per hour) and waves four to six feet high.
Partly cloudy and scattered rains along coast of Quintana Roo, with winds from northeast at 20 to 30 km.
